sections.h2: How can I sell a house fast in East Point, Georgia?
sections.html:
You can list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept an offer from a cash buyer, and the right route depends on the condition of the house and the date you need to close. East Point sits inside Fulton County, so the property tax and recording steps below follow Fulton County and Georgia rules.

A listing works best when the house is clean, repaired and priced close to what nearby homes bring. Selling it yourself saves the agent's fee but leaves marketing, showings, contract terms and negotiation with you. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, which cuts out repairs and open houses. The tradeoff is that an as-is offer usually lands below a polished retail sale.

  • Listing with an agent: widest buyer pool, but buyer financing, appraisals and repair requests set the timeline.
  • Selling yourself: you control the price and the paperwork, and you carry all of the marketing.
  • Cash offer: fewer moving parts and a closing date you pick, with a lower price as the usual cost.

Pull together the deed, your most recent East Point and Fulton County tax bills, any mortgage payoff letter and a list of known repairs before you talk to anyone. Those four items answer most of what a buyer or title attorney will ask first.

More than half of East Point households rent, so tenant-occupied houses are a normal part of local sales. If yours has a tenant, check the lease end date and any deposit you hold before you set a closing date. The median home value is a citywide midpoint, so a house in a historic district near downtown and a ranch on a larger lot farther out can sit well apart from it.

sections.h2: What is East Point like for someone buying a house there?
sections.html:
East Point is a railroad-born city just south of Atlanta, and its own city profile stresses short trips to the airport and downtown. The profile says the name comes from the eastern end of the Atlanta & West Point Railroad, that the settlement began in 1870 with 16 families, and that the city was chartered in 1887.

The city describes itself as five minutes from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport and ten minutes from downtown Atlanta, with MARTA bus and rail service and light traffic. It lists more than 25 neighborhoods. Streets around the historic downtown have tree-lined blocks with bungalows, cottages and Cape Cod homes. Farther out, brick ranch houses on bigger yards with garages or basements are common, and newer construction fills in other areas.

  • Walkability to the downtown district is a selling point for the older blocks.
  • Yard size, garages and basements are the features the city highlights for the outer neighborhoods.
  • Camp Creek Marketplace, with more than a million square feet of retail and commercial space, anchors shopping on the west side.
  • Sumner Park holds the velodrome that the city calls the only one of its kind in the state.

When you write a listing or speak with a buyer, lead with whichever of these fits your street. A buyer comparing East Point with other close-in suburbs wants to hear the airport, MARTA and downtown distances first.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax on an East Point house?
sections.html:
Two bills arrive for an East Point house: one from the City of East Point and a separate one from Fulton County. The city's finance page explains that values come from the Fulton County Board of Assessors and the millage rate for the city portion is adopted by the East Point City Council.

The tax year runs January 1 through December 31. East Point says statements are generally mailed in the fall with payment due 60 days after mailing, and the exact due date is printed on the statement. For 2026 the state approved a one-time Homeowner Tax Relief Grant, worth up to $18,000 off assessed taxable value for homes with an approved homestead exemption, and the city says the credit appears automatically on the city bill. It does not apply to rental, commercial or personal property.

On the county side, Fulton County sends a Notice of Assessment each year and gives owners 45 days to appeal the value, not the tax amount. For 2026 the appeal deadline for most owners was July 31, 2026, so that window has closed. Fulton County also kept its general fund rate at 8.87 mills in an October 7, 2026 vote, according to its news release.

  • City bill, payments and city homestead questions: East Point Finance Department, Property Tax Division.
  • Values, notices and appeals: Fulton County Board of Assessors at fultonassessor.org.
  • Proration of the current year's taxes between you and the buyer: your closing attorney.

sections.h2: What do East Point's short-term rental rules mean for a seller?
sections.html:
East Point requires a permit before a house is listed on a site like Airbnb or VRBO, and the permit renews every year. If you have been renting the house nightly, find out where the permit and the tax filings stand before you accept an offer.

The city defines a short-term rental as a residential unit rented for 29 days or less. Its FAQ lists a $75 homestay license and a $150 whole-house lodging license, and says operators owe an 8 percent monthly hotel/motel tax, with the prior month due on the 20th. Whole-house rentals are allowed only in a short list of zoning districts that includes R1A, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-T and CR. The city reported 65 permitted short-term rentals in 2025. Violations carry fines of $50 to $1,000 per offense, and each day can count as a separate offense.

A buyer or lender may ask for proof that the rental history is clean. Ask the Planning and Community Development Department whether any open complaints or unpaid hotel/motel tax sit on the address, and settle them first.

sections.h2: What does Georgia require when the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Georgia's Department of Revenue says the real estate transfer tax must be paid before a deed can be recorded with the clerk of superior court. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 of the price and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100.

The seller is the party liable under the statute, O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10, though the sales contract often assigns it to the buyer. The transfer tax declaration, Form PT-61, is filed electronically through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority. Your closing attorney normally handles that filing and the deed.

Read the contract line that says who pays the transfer tax before you sign. Then ask the closing attorney for a written estimate of every seller charge, including the mortgage payoff, the prorated property tax and any code or rental-tax balances the city shows against the address.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer suit an East Point house?
sections.html:
A cash offer suits a house when time, condition or a complicated situation makes the normal listing path slow or costly. Common East Point examples are an inherited house nobody wants to maintain, a tenant-occupied rental, a former short-term rental with loose ends, or a house that needs more repair than a retail buyer will accept.

  • You need a closing date set by you rather than by a buyer's lender.
  • The house needs roof, plumbing, foundation or cosmetic work you do not want to fund.
  • You are managing the sale from out of state or on behalf of an estate.

Compare any offer against what a repaired listing could realistically bring after the agent's fee and the repair bill. Ask for the offer in writing, confirm who pays closing costs and the transfer tax, and keep the right to decline.

faqs.q: Can I sell my East Point house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer will usually purchase the house in its current condition. A buyer who uses a mortgage may still ask for repairs after an inspection or appraisal.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax on an East Point sale?
faqs.a: The statute makes the seller liable, but the sales contract often moves it to the buyer. The Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100. Check the contract and the closing statement.

faqs.q: Where do I find my East Point property tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the City of East Point Finance Department for the city bill and Fulton County for the county bill, because the two are billed separately. Fulton values and notices are online at fultonassessor.org.

faqs.q: Does the 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant apply to a rental house?
faqs.a: No. East Point's finance page says the grant covers homeowners with an approved 2026 homestead exemption and does not apply to rental, commercial or personal property. Eligible owners get a credit on the city bill, not a check.

faqs.q: Can I sell an East Point house that has a tenant in it?
faqs.a: Yes. More than half of East Point households rent, so tenant-occupied sales are common. Review the lease end date and deposit, and tell any buyer, including a cash buyer, that the unit is occupied before you agree on a price.
